## Old Faithful {.divider data-number="01"}

## Historically, you own both halves

- Shiny defines the **UI** and the **server**
- One language, one mental model
- The UI vocabulary is *whatever Shiny ships*

## The app {.code-slide}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{.r filename="app.R"}
ui <- page_sidebar(
  sidebar = sidebar(
    sliderInput("bins", "Bins:",
                min = 1, max = 50,
                value = 30)
  ),
  plotOutput("distPlot")
)
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{.r filename="server"}
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    x <- faithful$waiting
    hist(x, breaks = input$bins)
  })
}
```
:::
:::

## Shiny React {.divider data-number="02"}

## Same server, your frontend {.code-slide}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{.tsx filename="app.tsx"}
const [n, setN] = useShinyInput(
  "bins", 30
);
const plot = useShinyOutputValue(
  "hist"
);

return <Slider value={n}
  onChange={setN} />;
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{.r filename="app.R"}
ui <- page_react_html("www/index.html")

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$hist <- reactive_output({
    req(input$bins)
    hist_data(x, input$bins)
  })
}
```
:::
:::
